messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: Identifiability issue in inla clarification
parts:
Hi INLA members,

I have a question regarding identifiability in INLA.

If my model formula is the following:

Y~ X+f(id1, "iid)+ f(id2, X, model="bym",graph)

Then is there any possibility for identifiability in INLA? Here I have the intercept term and also X as covariate also X as weight in random effect with id2.

Alokesh.

messages.author: 3eab71733027a24a
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Identifiability issue in inla clarification
parts:
the bym is a shorthand for

iid + besag

so if 'id1=id2', you'll have a perfect confounding

see the doc

inla.doc("bym")


'bym2' is a better version of 'bym'

messages.author: ab78e227e394cf1d
messages.subject: Re: [r-inla] Identifiability issue in inla clarification
parts:
Hi Havard,

Thank you!

Say the formula is

Y~X+f(id1, "iid)+ f(id2, X, model="besag",graph)

And id1 is not same as id2. In my model you can think of id1 as different map specific effect and id2 is for each map based on different spatial region which are same for each map. I think in besag already there is sum zero constraint by default. So, will there be any identifiable problem as the coefficient can be interpreted as (beta_{x}+ beta_{x,id2}) X;

Where beta_{x} for fixed effect and beta_{x,id2} for random effect. But if there is already zero sum constraint by default, will that resolve our issue for identifiability?

Alokesh

Also why should we use scale.model= TRUE?
